title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Dispute Cases involving Rural Land Contracting

articles.content_en:
Article 2: Where the parties voluntarily reach a written arbitration agreement, the People's Court hearing the case shall handle the matter by reference to the provisions of Articles 215 and 216 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.
Where the parties have not reached a written arbitration agreement, and one party applies to a rural land contracting arbitration institution for arbitration while the other party initiates an action, the People's Court shall accept the case and shall notify the arbitration institution in writing. However, where the other party has accepted the jurisdiction of arbitration and subsequently initiates an action, the People's Court shall not accept it.
Where a party is dissatisfied with the arbitration award and initiates an action within thirty days from the date of receipt of the award, the People's Court shall accept it.

Article 3: In a dispute over a contract agreement, the party that contracts out the land and the contracted party shall be the parties.
The "contracted party" as mentioned in the preceding paragraph refers to the farmer household that contracts rural land of the collective economic organization by way of household contracting, and the organization or individual that contracts rural land by other means.

Article 5: Where any term in a contract agreement concerning the withdrawal or adjustment of contracted land violates Articles 27, 28, and 31 of the Rural Land Contracting Law, that term shall be determined to be null and void.

Article 6: Disputes arising from the contract-awarding party's illegal withdrawal or adjustment of contracted land, or from the contract-awarding party's withdrawal of contracted land that the contracted party has abandoned or left uncultivated, shall be handled separately according to the following circumstances:
(1) where the contract-awarding party has not contracted the land out to another party, and the contracted party requests the return of the contracted land, the request shall be supported;
(2) where the contract-awarding party has contracted the land out to a third party, and the contracted party, naming the contract-awarding party and the third party as co-defendants, requests that the contract agreement signed by them be confirmed null and void, the return of the contracted land, and compensation for losses, the request shall be supported. However, where the circumstances are those of the contracted party's abandonment or leaving the land uncultivated, the claim for compensation for losses shall not be supported.
Where the third party referred to in item (2) of the preceding paragraph requests the party that has benefited to compensate it for its reasonable investment in the contracted land, the request shall be supported.

Article 7: Where the contract term stipulated in a contract agreement or recorded in a certificate of the right to land contractual management or other certificates is shorter than the term prescribed by the Rural Land Contracting Law, and the contracted party requests an extension, the request shall be supported.

Article 8: Where the contracted party, in violation of the provisions of Article 18 of the Rural Land Contracting Law, uses the contracted land for non-agricultural construction without approval in accordance with law or causes permanent damage to the contracted land, and the contract-awarding party requests the contracted party to cease the infringement, restore the land to its original condition, or compensate for losses, the request shall be supported.

Article 10: Where the return of contracted land by the contracted party does not conform to the procedures prescribed by Article 30 of the Rural Land Contracting Law, the return shall not be determined to be voluntary.

Article 12: Where the contract-awarding party coerces the contracted party into circulating the land management right to a third party, and the contracted party requests the rescission of the circulation contract concluded with the third party, the request shall be supported.
Where the contract-awarding party obstructs the contracted party from lawfully circulating the land management right, and the contracted party requests the removal of the obstruction and compensation for losses, the request shall be supported.

Article 13: Where the contracted party transfers its right to land contractual management without the consent of the contract-awarding party, the transfer contract shall be null and void, unless the contract-awarding party has no legal reason to withhold consent or delays in expressing its position.

Article 14: Where the contracted party lawfully circulates the land management right by lease, shareholding, or other means, and the contract-awarding party requests confirmation that the contract is null and void only on the ground that the land management right circulation contract was not submitted to it for archival filing, the request shall not be supported.

Article 15: Where a dispute arises over the provisions that the contracted party does not collect circulation price or pays fees to the other party, and the parties cannot reach an agreement on modification through consultation, and continued performance is obviously unfair, the People's Court may, according to the objective circumstances that have changed, handle the matter in accordance with the principle of fairness.

Article 16: Where the parties have not agreed on the term of circulation of the leased land or the agreement is unclear, the matter shall be handled by reference to Article 730 of the Civil Code. Except where the parties otherwise agree or the case involves forest land contracting, the time for returning the contracted land shall be after the end of the crop harvest period or before the beginning of the next cultivation period.
Where investments have been made to enhance the land's production capacity, and the other party requests the contracted party to provide corresponding compensation, the request shall be supported.

Article 17: Where the contract-awarding party or any other organization or individual, without authorization, intercepts or withholds the proceeds from contracting or the proceeds from the circulation of land management rights, and the contracted party requests their return, the request shall be supported.
Where the contract-awarding party or any other organization or individual claims set-off, the claim shall not be supported.
III. Handling of Disputes over Contracting by Other Means

Article 18: Where a member of the collective economic organization claims priority in contracting under conditions where the main contents such as the contract fee and the contract term are the same, the claim shall be supported. However, where the contract-awarding party has contracted the rural land out to an organization or individual outside the collective economic organization, and the matter has passed the democratic decision-making procedure prescribed by law and has been approved by the township (town) people's government, a claim of priority in contracting made after such approval shall not be supported.

Article 20: Where contracted land is lawfully expropriated, and the contracted party requests the contract-awarding party to pay the compensation fees for above-ground attachments and young crops that have been received, the request shall be supported.
Where the contracted party has circulated the land management right to a third party by lease, shareholding, or other means, unless the parties otherwise agree, the compensation fee for young crops shall belong to the person who actually made the investment, and the compensation fee for above-ground attachments shall belong to the owner of the attachments.

Article 21: Where contracted land is lawfully expropriated, and a household contracted party that gives up unified resettlement requests the contract-awarding party to pay the resettlement subsidy fees that have been received, the request shall be supported.

Article 22: A rural collective economic organization, villagers' committee, or villagers' group may, in accordance with the democratic decision-making procedure prescribed by law, decide to distribute within the collective economic organization the land compensation fees already received. Where a person who already has the status of a member of the collective economic organization at the time when the land expropriation compensation and resettlement plan is determined requests payment of the corresponding share, the request shall be supported, except where local regulations, autonomous regulations and separate regulations, and local government rules filed for the record with the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress and the State Council provide otherwise for the method of distribution of land compensation fees within a rural collective economic organization.

Article 23: In household contracting of forest land, where the successor of the contracted party requests to continue contracting within the contract term, the request shall be supported.
In contracting by other means, where the successor of the contracted party or the person who assumes its rights and obligations requests to continue contracting within the contract term, the request shall be supported.
V. Other Provisions

Article 24: When hearing dispute cases involving Article 5, Article 6, paragraph 1, item (2) and paragraph 2, and Article 15 of this Interpretation, the People's Court shall focus on mediation. Where necessary, it may entrust a people's mediation organization to conduct mediation.

Article 25: This Interpretation shall come into force on September 1, 2005. The provisions of this Interpretation shall apply to cases of first instance accepted after its coming into force.
Where judicial interpretations already in effect before its coming into force are inconsistent with this Interpretation, this Interpretation shall prevail.
